ideas.idea: SmartMoving-native outbound lead engine for independent moving companies
ideas.description: An outbound lead-generation service for residential moving companies. It monitors newly listed homes, finds and verifies each seller’s contact details, sends personalized outreach on the mover’s behalf, and routes interested replies directly into SmartMoving. The proposed version would sell smaller exclusive ZIP-code territories with done-for-you onboarding.
ideas.traction: $7,615 MRR from 8 active subscriptions (TrustMRR snapshot at time of research)
ideas.customer: Independent US residential moving companies using SmartMoving, roughly 2–10 trucks, one metro
ideas.wedge: SmartMoving-native lead delivery + smaller exclusive ZIP territories + done-for-you onboarding
ideas.why: High ARPU, tiny required customer count, identifiable buyers, direct-sales friendly, licensable inputs, measurable ROI
ideas.risk: The listing-to-booked-move conversion may be too weak to sustain repeatable ROI; incumbent could add the same integration wedge

ideas.idea: White-label mobile app performance reporting for ASO and mobile-growth agencies
ideas.description: A reporting hub for agencies that manage multiple mobile-app clients. It connects each client's Apple App Store Connect, Google Play Console and selected acquisition sources, continuously normalizes performance data, and automatically produces branded client reports, portals and alerts instead of requiring analysts to rebuild dashboards or monthly decks.
ideas.incumbent: Easy App Reports by Beyond Analytics
ideas.traction: $3,474 MRR from 22 active subscriptions; $164,908 all-time revenue; 1-person bootstrapped team (TrustMRR, Aug 29 2026)
ideas.customer: ASO and mobile-app growth agencies with ~5–50 active client apps and recurring retainers
ideas.wedge: Own the client-delivery layer: white-label portals, scheduled branded reports, KPI goals, annotations and commentary—rather than selling generic BI/data connectors
ideas.why: Verified low-customer-count B2B revenue, official/replicable data sources, enumerable agency buyers, recurring workflow pain, strong expansion pricing and a fast concierge validation path
ideas.risk: Agencies may already be satisfied with AppTweak/Appfigures/Looker Studio; Apple/Google permissions and source-report delays could make onboarding/support too heavy

ideas.idea: AI Meta-ad comment-to-booking agent for home-improvement companies
ideas.description: A conversion agent for home-improvement companies already running Facebook and Instagram ads. It watches ad comments and DMs, hides obvious spam, answers approved buyer questions, detects high intent, qualifies prospects in private messages, books estimates, and writes the lead plus conversation context into the company's CRM.
ideas.traction: $8,363 MRR from 38 active subscriptions; $56,911 all-time revenue; Stripe-verified TrustMRR snapshot on 2026-09-07
ideas.customer: US roofing companies with ~5–50 employees, meaningful Meta ad spend, and GoHighLevel/agency-managed lead workflows
ideas.wedge: Meta-first + roofing-first; turn paid-ad comments into qualified DMs and booked estimates in GoHighLevel, with done-for-you setup and revenue attribution
ideas.why: Strong verified ARPU with few incumbent customers, official/replicable platform APIs, easy-to-enumerate buyers, one job can pay for months of SaaS, and the core workflow can be concierge-validated before building broadly
ideas.risk: ManyChat/HighLevel/native Meta tools may already be good enough, or Meta permissions may constrain comment-to-DM automation; the thesis fails if qualified comments do not become incremental booked estimates

ideas.idea: Statement-first travel commission reconciliation and advisor-payout SaaS
ideas.description: A back-office tool for travel agencies that ingests the supplier commission statements they already receive as PDF, Excel, CSV, email or pasted text. It extracts booking and commission lines, matches them against the agency's expected bookings, flags missing or incorrect payments, calculates advisor splits, and produces a reconciled payout report and audit trail without requiring the agency to replace its CRM.
ideas.incumbent: Sion (with supporting validation from Toggle Travel, Wihemi Travel and Trip Ledger)
ideas.traction: Sion acquired by Bilt for $30M on 11 Mar 2026; Sion says 8,000+ advisors and $7B+ booking revenue managed. Toggle starts at $350/mo; Wihemi $169/mo. JourneyFuse separately shows ~$6.38k verified MRR / 300 subscriptions on TrustMRR.
ideas.customer: US independent travel agencies and small host agencies with ~10–75 advisors, roughly $2M–$30M annual booking volume, multiple suppliers, and manual/spreadsheet-heavy commission reconciliation.
ideas.wedge: Statement-first instead of CRM/GDS-first: upload supplier statements plus a simple booking export, reconcile automatically with a human-review exception queue, then add only the integrations repeated customers actually demand.
ideas.why: Exceptionally strong proof of willingness to pay and strategic value, easy-to-identify B2B buyers, recurring financial workflow, $300–$1,000+ plausible ARPU, and a concierge MVP that can validate extraction/matching before building deep integrations.
ideas.risk: Statement variability and ambiguous booking matching could force customer-specific integrations and turn the product into a services-heavy back-office implementation; incumbents may already solve enough of the problem.
